title: Possession and giving
subtitle: belongings, estate, proprietor, hand down
summary: Learn the nouns for what people own, the words for owners and tenants, the verbs of giving such as donate and allocate, and the phrasal verbs like hand over and hand down.

lesson.heading: Words for what people own
rows: All his possessions were destroyed in the terrible fire.
smaller personal things - bag, camera, coat; always plural
Don't leave any of your belongings here; we've had a few thefts.
houses, land, etc. in a general sense
He's only 14; he's too young to own property.
a building or piece of land
She owns some valuable properties in the town centre.

lesson.heading: The three meanings of estate
lesson.text: **Estate** in the singular has three common uses: a group of houses built together, a big area of private land, and all of someone's wealth when they die.

examples.note: an area with a large number of houses or flats built close together at the same time

examples.text: She owns a huge **estate** in Scotland.
examples.note: a big area of private land and the buildings on it

examples.text: After his death, his **estate** was calculated at 10 million euros.

lesson.heading: People connected with ownership
rows: the owner of a shop or business (formal; owner is less formal)
the person who rents a property from the owner
to become the owner of something after someone's death
lesson.note: The proprietor of this restaurant is a friend of mine. Do you own this house? No, we're just tenants. He inherited a big house in the country when his parents died.

lesson.heading: Verbs of giving and their patterns
rows: provide somebody with something, or provide something for somebody; supply is often used for selling contexts
present somebody with something - a formal gift
give money or goods, especially to a fund or an institution
give somebody a share of something officially
give somebody money to live on
give money or things in your will after you die
give money if somebody completes a challenge

lesson.heading: Giving in use
lesson.text: Watch the prepositions and objects. **Cater for** takes *for*; **supply** takes *with*; **allocate** normally has a person and a thing.

examples.text: The river **provides** the village **with** water. / The river **provides** water **for** the village.
Jakes Ltd **supplies** our school **with** paper and other items.
It gives me pleasure to **present** you **with** this gift from us all.
Would you like to **contribute/donate** something to the children's hospital fund?
You've been **allocated** room 24. Here's your key.
The school restaurant **caters for** 500 people every day.
I'm running a marathon next week for a cancer charity. Will you **sponsor** me?

lesson.heading: Phrasal verbs connected with giving
rows: give something to someone who takes charge of it
I had to hand over the keys to my office to the new person.
I didn't want to let go of my bike but I had no money.
The people from the charity handed out stickers for everyone to wear.
I had a banjo once, but I gave it away.
pass on from one generation to the next
This vase has been handed down from generation to generation.

lesson.text: Donate is for large gifts to institutions - *she donated all her books to the library* - while contribute works for money given to a fund of any size.

exercises.prompt: He became a multi-millionaire and bought a huge ___ in the country.
exercises.explanation: Estate can mean a big area of private land and the buildings on it.

exercises.prompt: I left some of my ___ in the changing room at the gym and they were stolen.
exercises.explanation: Belongings are smaller personal things such as a bag, camera or coat.

exercises.prompt: She sold all her ___ and travelled around the world for a year.
It's often difficult for young couples to buy ___ and they have to rent a place instead.
exercises.explanation: Property (uncountable) is used generally for houses, land and so on.

exercises.prompt: Some of the ___ in this street have sold for more than five million euros this year.
exercises.explanation: A property (countable) is a building or piece of land, so the plural is properties.

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence beginning with the right verb.

pairs.left: A millionaire ___ his entire library to the school.
The director was ___ the best parking place.
My mother's cousin ___ me 5,000 pounds in her will.
A farmer nearby ___ us with logs for the fire.
When I retired they ___ me with a camera.

exercises.prompt: The oldest son ___ the house when his father died.
exercises.explanation: To inherit is to become the owner of something after someone's death.

exercises.prompt: *Yes, that's right. I pay rent every month.* Which question produced this answer?
exercises.explanation: A tenant rents a property from a landlord or landlady.

exercises.prompt: *OK, I'll give you one euro for every kilometre you run.* Which question produced this answer?
options: Will you sponsor me in a race for charity?
Will you donate your books to the library?
Have you been allocated a room?
Did you hand over the keys?
exercises.explanation: To sponsor someone is to give money if they complete a challenge such as a run.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrasal verb with its meaning.

pairs.right: give something to the person taking charge of it
distribute to a lot of people
pass on from one generation to the next

exercises.statement: A landlord is someone who rents a flat from the owner.
exercises.explanation: A landlord is the owner of rented property; the person who rents it is the tenant.

exercises.prompt: Toby Fatcatt's story: is each word about owning or about giving?
Put the words in order to describe a family heirloom.
exercises.answer: This vase has been handed down from generation to generation.
exercises.explanation: Hand down means to pass something on from one generation to the next.
